entities.summary: Maxine Jones is an American singer, songwriter, actress and businesswoman, best known as a founding member of the R&B-pop group En Vogue, one of the world's best-selling girl groups of all time. She sang lead vocals on the group's signature singles "My Lovin' " and "Don't Let Go (Love)", both of which garnered international success and sold over a million copies. Throughout her career, Jones has sold over 20 million records with En Vogue. Her work has earned her several awards and nominations, including two American Music Awards, a Billboard Music Award, four MTV Video Music Awards, and four Soul Train Music Awards.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a founding member of En Vogue, Maxine Jones contributed to the group's success with over 20 million records sold worldwide, earning her multiple awards and nominations. Her work had significant regional impact in the music industry, particularly in the R&B-pop genre.
